verdict.guard_found: none in this repo. The only check is ensure_allowed (acl.py:8-10), which aborts with 403 on failure and is used at views.py:26, but it authorizes whatever g.user is set to. At views.py:18, require_allowed (is_allowed, acl.py:4-5) returns a bool that is discarded, so DELETE /files/<fid> has no effective check at all. Nothing in the repo verifies or signs X-Session-User-Verified (views.py:12). The only possible mitigation is an upstream proxy that strips and sets the header, which the repo cannot show.
verdict.reason: views.py:12 sets g.user straight from the request header with no verification, and views.py:26 uses ensure_allowed (acl.py:8-10) to gate rename on that value, so any client that can reach the app and send a chosen header can impersonate a grant holder. The trace is partly wrong: views.py:18 is not an authorization point, because require_allowed/is_allowed (acl.py:4-5) returns a bool that is discarded, so DELETE is unauthorized for every caller regardless of identity, which is a stronger bug than the candidate describes. The verdict depends on the app being directly reachable, which this repo cannot confirm.
